info.title: HubSpot MCP REST API
info.description: REST data plane for the HubSpot CRM: companies, contacts, deals, pipelines, tickets, conversations and property definitions, plus the gated writes. Reads exist so a shell-capable client can curl | jq bulk payloads without them crossing the LLM context window, and every read also accepts format=text to get the same markdown the MCP tool renders. Writes are validated with the MCP tools own exported Zod schemas, so the two surfaces cannot drift. Every deal endpoint needs the crm.objects.deals.read scope: an already-connected user must reconnect from the dashboard, and until they do the 403 body names both the needed and the granted scopes.

get.summary: Get most recently active HubSpot companies
get.description: Companies sorted by last-modified date. Mirrors the MCP tool `getActiveCompanies`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum records to return (default 10, max 100).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Response shape. Defaults to raw upstream JSON; text/plain/markdown render the same output the MCP tool returns. Accept: text/plain does the same thing.

400.description: Request or query parameters failed validation. `issues` carries the flattened Zod field errors.

get.summary: Get activity history for a HubSpot company
get.description: Notes, calls, meetings and tasks associated with the company — never deals, which have their own endpoint. The engagement fan-out is capped at 100 details and `omitted` reports how many were left out, so a truncated timeline is never mistaken for the whole history. Mirrors the MCP tool `getCompanyActivity`.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Response shape. Defaults to raw upstream JSON; text/plain/markdown render the same output the MCP tool returns. Accept: text/plain does the same thing.

get.summary: List the deals associated with a HubSpot company
get.description: The only route from a company to its deal IDs: a company record carries num_associated_deals as a plain company property, so without this the by-ID deal endpoints cannot be reached from a company. The association scan is bounded at 5,000 IDs — truncated:true means associatedCount is a floor rather than a count. Needs the crm.objects.deals.read scope. Mirrors the MCP tool `getCompanyDeals`.

parameters.description: HubSpot company ID.

get.description: criteria=default matches tickets closed or last-modified within the last day; criteria=Closed filters on the pipeline stage. The datetime filters go upstream as epoch milliseconds — HubSpot 400s on ISO-8601 — so they are never built from a date string here. Mirrors the MCP tool `getTickets`.

parameters.name: criteria
parameters.description: Which ticket set to return.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum records to return (default 50, max 100).

parameters.name: maxRetries
parameters.description: Retry attempts on 429/5xx (exponential backoff). Capped at 3: the total sleep is retryDelay * (2^maxRetries - 1) seconds, and an unbounded budget would hold the socket open for hours during exactly the rate limiting that triggered the retries.

parameters.name: retryDelay
parameters.description: Initial retry delay in seconds; doubles each attempt. Capped at 2, which keeps the worst-case sleep at 14 seconds.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Response shape. Defaults to raw upstream JSON; text/plain/markdown render the same output the MCP tool returns. Accept: text/plain does the same thing.

post.summary: Create a HubSpot note and optionally attach it to a record
post.description: Accepts a body up to 5 MB, which is the point: a long note travels straight to HubSpot instead of through a tool call. The engagement is created standalone and then attached with a v4 default association, so the response reports the attachment outcome separately: association.attempted without association.attached means the record exists but sits on no timeline. Mirrors the MCP tool `createNote`.

201.description: The engagement was created. This is 201 even when the association failed, because the record does exist — check association.attached before reporting it as on the timeline.

400.description: Request or query parameters failed validation. `issues` carries the flattened Zod field errors.

403.description: No connection for this service on the account, or the provider denied the call.

hs_timestamp.description: Activity time as ISO-8601 or epoch milliseconds. Defaults to now — omitting it is the most common HubSpot engagement-create failure, so this endpoint fills it in.

associateToObjectType.description: Record type to attach the activity to. Must be given together with associateToObjectId.

associateToObjectId.description: ID of the record to attach the activity to. Must be given together with associateToObjectType.

CrmObject.description: A raw HubSpot CRM object: id, properties, createdAt, updatedAt.

created.description: false means a company of that name already existed and nothing was written.
false means a matching contact already existed and nothing was written.
Always true — deals are never deduped.

association.description: Outcome of the optional timeline attachment. attempted:true with attached:false is an ORPHANED engagement — it exists but appears on no record timeline until it is associated.

error.description: Why the attachment failed, when it did.

omitted.description: Associated engagements beyond the 100-detail cap. Non-zero means this is not the whole timeline.

associatedCount.description: IDs the association scan found before limit was applied. A FLOOR when truncated is true.

requestedCount.description: IDs this call asked HubSpot to read: min(associatedCount, limit).

truncated.description: The association scan hit its page bound, so associatedCount is not a total.

nextAfter.description: Cursor for the next page, when there is one.
